title: Rigveda 7.12: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.12: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.12 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 500r-500v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.12.1-2 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 2, varga 15); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 500r
translation.original_text:
1aga̍nma ma̱hā nama̍sā̱ yavi̍ṣṭha̱ṁ yo dī̱dāya̱ sami̍ddha̱ḥ sve du̍ro̱ṇe | ci̱trabhā̍nu̱ṁ roda̍sī a̱ntar u̱rvī svā̍hutaṁ vi̱śvata̍ḥ pra̱tyañca̍m ||
2sa ma̱hnā viśvā̍ duri̱tāni̍ sā̱hvān a̱gniḥ ṣṭa̍ve̱ dama̱ ā jā̱tave̍dāḥ | sa no̍ rakṣiṣad duri̱tād a̍va̱dyād a̱smān gṛ̍ṇa̱ta u̱ta no̍ ma̱ghona̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1WE with great reverence have approached The Youngest who hath shone forth well-kindled in his dwelling, With wondrous light between wide earth and heaven, well-worshipped, looking forth in all directions.
2Through his great might o'ercoming all misfortunes, praised in the house is Agni Jâtavedas. May he protect us from disgrace and trouble, both us who laud him and our noble patrons.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 500r (numbered 21r by the scribe) (OPenn image 500, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.11.2 ‹-it mānuṣāsaḥ yasya devaiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 500v (numbered 21v by the scribe), begins in RV 7.12.3 ‹su-saṇanāni santu yūyam pāta›. Verses 7.12.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1aganma | mahā | namasā | yaviṣṭham | yaḥ | dīdāya | sam-iddhaḥ | sve | duroṇe | ci tra-bhānum | rodasī iti | antaḥ | urvī iti | su-āhutam | pratyañcam
2saḥ | mahnā | viśvā | duḥ-itāni | sāhvān | agniḥ | stave | dame | ā | jāta-vedāḥ | saḥ | naḥ | rakṣiṣat | duḥ-itāt | avadyāt | asmān | gṛṇataḥ | uta | naḥ | maghonaḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 7.12.3 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 2, varga 15); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 500v
translation.original_text: <sup>3</sup>tvaṁ varu̍ṇa u̱ta mi̱tro a̍gne̱ tvāṁ va̍rdhanti ma̱tibhi̱r vasi̍ṣṭhāḥ | tve vasu̍ suṣaṇa̱nāni̍ santu yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>3</sup>O Agni, thou art Varuṇa and Mitra: Vasishṭhas with their holy hymns exalt thee. With thee be most abundant gain of treasure. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 500v (numbered 21v by the scribe) (OPenn image 501, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.12.3 ‹su-saṇanāni santu yūyam pāta›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 501r (numbered 22r by the scribe), begins in RV 7.15.1 ‹juhuta haviḥ yaḥ naḥ›. Verse 7.12.3 ends on this page; 7.12.3 begins on fol. 500r (numbered 21r by the scribe).
